title: Build and optimize clean Al(110) slab
action: Construct a periodic Al(110) surface slab model with a p(6×3) surface unit cell, 6 atomic layers, and a vacuum gap of at least 10 Å. Perform a variable-cell relaxation (ions + cell) using DFT (GGA-PBE, ultrasoft pseudopotentials) to obtain the optimized clean surface geometry and its total energy.
description: Slab geometry optimization required as reference for all subsequent adsorption calculations.

title: Optimize gas-phase AlCl and AlCl3 molecules
action: Isolate a single AlCl molecule and a single AlCl3 molecule in large supercells (same cell dimensions as the slab, keeping vacuum) and relax their atomic positions with the same DFT settings. Obtain their optimized total energies.
description: Gas-phase total energies are needed for computing adsorption and desorption energies.

title: Optimize all required adsorbed configurations
action: Place each adsorbate (AlCl, Cl, AlCl2, AlCl3, Al) on the optimized Al(110) slab in the specific co-adsorption arrangements described in the paper (AlCl at fourfold hollow; AlCl+Cl; AlCl2+Cl; AlCl2 at fourfold hollow; AlCl3 at bridge; AlCl+AlCl; AlCl+AlCl2; AlCl2+AlCl2; and product configurations such as Al+Cl, AlCl2, AlCl3, AlCl2+Al, AlCl3+Al, AlCl3+AlCl). For each system, perform a full geometry optimization (ions only, keeping slab bottom layers fixed if desired) using the same DFT settings. Record the total energy of each optimized system.
description: All surface+adsorbate total energies are required to compute adsorption/desorption energies and elementary step reaction energies.

title: Locate transition states for elementary steps
action: For each elementary surface reaction (A2, A3, A4, B2/C2, B3, C3), use the optimized reactant and product configurations from Step 3 to locate the transition state on the potential energy surface using the LST/QST method or any equivalent transition-state search algorithm (e.g., NEB, CI-NEB), all within the same DFT settings. Confirm each TS by a single imaginary frequency. For each step, record the total energy of the transition state and derive the forward activation energy E_a = E(TS) − E(reactants).
description: Transition state searches required to obtain activation energies for the elementary steps.

title: Compute adsorption and desorption energies
action: Using the total energies from the clean slab, gas-phase molecules, and adsorbate configurations, calculate the adsorption energy of AlCl on Al(110) as E_ads(AlCl) = E(slab+AlCl) - E(slab) - E(AlCl); the desorption energy of AlCl as E_des(AlCl) = -E_ads(AlCl); and the desorption energy of AlCl3 as E_des(AlCl3) = E(slab) + E(AlCl3) - E(slab+AlCl3). Write the computed values to ads_des_energies.json.
description: Contains three energy values in eV: adsorption energy of AlCl, desorption energy of AlCl, and desorption energy of AlCl3.

title: Compute elementary reaction and activation energies
action: For each elementary surface reaction step (A2: AlCl(∗) → Al(∗)+Cl(∗); A3: AlCl(∗)+Cl(∗) → AlCl2(∗); A4: AlCl2(∗)+Cl(∗) → AlCl3(∗); B2 (also C2): 2AlCl(∗) → AlCl2(∗)+Al(∗); B3: AlCl2(∗)+AlCl(∗) → AlCl3(∗)+Al(∗); C3: 2AlCl2(∗) → AlCl(∗)+AlCl3(∗)), compute the reaction energy as E(products) − E(reactants) using the total energies of the optimized reactant and product configurations, and the forward activation energy E_a = E(TS) − E(reactants) from the transition-state calculations. Write the results to reaction_energies.csv with columns step_id, reaction_energy (eV), and activation_energy (eV).
description: CSV file with columns step_id (string), reaction_energy (float eV), and activation_energy (float eV).

title: Compile mechanism-level energetics
action: For each mechanism A, B, C, sum the surface-only reaction energies using the step energies from the elementary steps. Then add the adsorption contributions (three times E_ads(AlCl) for A and B; four times for C) and the desorption contributions (once for AlCl3 in all three, and once for AlCl in mechanism C). Obtain the surface-only reaction energy and the general reaction energy for each mechanism. Write the results to general_energies.json.
description: JSON object with keys mechanism_A, mechanism_B, mechanism_C, each containing surface_only_energy (float) and general_energy (float), both in eV.
